We expand the parentheses using the **distributive property**:

$\blueD A(B+C)=\blueD A\cdot B+\blueD A\cdot C$

We can also think about the problem using an area model:

[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: Two rectangles of different sizes make up a larger rectangle. At the left, a rectangle has the width of negative q and a length of negative five q squared. At the rectangle on the right, it has a width of negative five with a length of negative five q squared.

hints.content:
Here's how the solution goes, algebraically:

$\begin{align}
&\phantom{=}\goldE{-5q^2}(-q-5)
\\\\
&=\goldE{-5q^2}(-q)+(\goldE{-5q^2})(-5)
\\\\
&=5q^3+25q^2
\end{align}$

Here's how the solution looks in terms of the area model:

Inside of this rectangle is five q cubed. At the rectangle on the right, it has a width of negative five with a length of negative five q squared. Inside of this rectangle is twenty five q squared.
